title: Define operational contracts for multi-tenant latency degradation, graceful fallbacks, and canary thresholds
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Summary: Define a set of operational contracts (SLO bands, per-tenant error budgets, and automated canary/rollback thresholds) specifically tailored for Redwood's multi-tenant Hosted endpoints. This PRD clarifies acceptance criteria, rollout gating logic, and the observable signals required to perform safe progressive rollouts and automated graceful degradation when capacity or model quality regressions occur.

Context: Several recent experiments with model swaps and kernel upgrades showed uneven latency regressions for a small subset of tenants and workload shapes. Existing SLO docs are service-level only; we need explicit per-tenant and per-workload SLOs plus automated gates so console rollouts and runtime orchestrator can make deterministic decisions (throttle, fallback to smaller model, enable degraded path).

Scope:
- Define latency SLO bands (p50/p95/p99) for three workload classes (interactive chat, batch/completions, embedding fetch) and per-tenant burst handling.
- Define per-tenant error budget accounting (windowing and burn-rate rules) and how it maps to canary/rollback decisions.
- Specify automated canary thresholds that combine latency, error-rate, and quality regressions (where quality signal exists).
- Document graceful degradation strategies and when they're triggered: model-variant fallback, KV-cache bypass, request dropping vs. priority routing.
- Integration points: Console rollout gating UI, runtime autoscaler hooks, incident runbooks, and alerting dashboards.

Out of scope: SDK surface changes, billing model changes, and Dedicated/private deployment policy variations (these will be covered in follow-up tickets).
acceptance_criteria: Define three workload classes with explicit SLO targets: interactive chat (p95 <= 150ms, p99 <= 400ms), completions (p95 <= 250ms, p99 <= 800ms), embeddings (p95 <= 75ms, p99 <= 200ms)

Document per-tenant error budget semantics: 28-day rolling window, 99.9% availability target for premium tenants, 99.5% for standard tenants; define burn-rate thresholds for warnings and automated throttles
Specify canary gating rule set: a canary is considered degraded if p95 latency increases by >20% AND request error-rate increases by >0.3 percentage points over baseline in a 10 minute window

Create rollout decision matrix mapping signal combinations to actions: immediate rollback, pause rollout and notify, continue with throttled traffic, degrade to model-variant or enable caching-only responses

Define automated graceful degradation flows: priority routing (tiered tokens), model-variant fallback semantics (compatibility and output constraints), and explicit graceful-deny with structured error payloads
Integrate gates with Console: a) show per-canary SLO delta, b) show per-tenant error budget burn rates, c) enable operator override and manual rollback
Provide sample dashboards and alerts: pre-configured Grafana/Console views for p50/p95/p99, error-rate by tenant, and canary burn-rate spike alerts
Hold a stakeholder review with eng/reliability/design where sign-off is captured in ticket comments
Add at least one end-to-end dry-run canary using a non-critical model where the automated gate triggers and records the expected behavior in the deployment log
notes: Design trade-off: tighter p95 targets for interactive chat increase risk of false positives during short-lived infra noise — will pair with short suppression windows and burn-rate smoothing
We prefer combined-signal canary gates to reduce single-metric flakiness (e.g., CPU spike only) — eng wants to include kernel-level metrics in later iteration
Operational constraint: per-tenant SLO accounting requires tagging at ingress and additional metrics storage costs; finance flagged for sizing impact
Related work: ENG-4921 (per-request tenant-tagging), ENG-5132 (canary orchestration engine), PM-25719 (model fallback policy)
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): finalize SLO numbers, wire per-tenant tagging (ENG-4921), basic console surface for canary metrics
Phase 2 (3 weeks): implement canary gating logic in orchestration engine (ENG-5132), automated rollback actions, and sample dry-run canary
Phase 3 (2 weeks): add graceful degradation flows, integrate model-variant fallbacks, and end-to-end test with telemetry verification
Rollout: initial internal rollout -> opt-in customers -> default enabled for new deployments after 4 weeks of stable signals
